TITLE: TSMC Q3 2026: AI outruns capacity, margins are the debate
SOURCE_LINE: Source: Syz Research, Bloomberg, company filings, analyst research notes of 15 October 2026
QUOTE: Demand is extremely robust.” … “There is no ceiling for [TSMC’s] profitability.
QUOTE_WHO: C.C. Wei, Chief Executive Officer, Q3 2026 earnings call, 15 October 2026 (as reproduced in analyst research notes)

TAKEAWAYS.label: Beat
TAKEAWAYS.text: Revenue of USD 46.7bn (+41% year on year) and EPS TWD 29.43 both beat consensus by about 3%.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Raised
TAKEAWAYS.text: The Q4 guide of USD 52.3–54.3bn sits 5–8% above prior consensus, locking in 44% growth for 2026.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Watch
TAKEAWAYS.text: Gross margin of 66.4% missed by 0.6 points on 2nm dilution; overseas fabs cost 3–4 points in 2027.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Valuation
TAKEAWAYS.text: 19.7x forward earnings: 16% above the 2005 to 2026 average, well below the one-year average of 23.3x.

H_P1: AI now sets the pace, not the cycle
P1_PARAGRAPH: The quarter matters less for the 3% beat than for what management said about the years ahead. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) now expects revenue from artificial intelligence (AI) accelerators to grow faster than the mid-to-high 50s% annual pace it guided for 2024 to 2029, and plans to more than double its 2-nanometre (2nm) capacity in 2027. Demand is no longer the question: the debate has moved to how much of it reaches margins and free cash flow.
C1_TITLE: TSM: Q3 2026 results and Q4 guide vs. consensus
C1_SUB: Surprise vs. pre-results consensus in %, gross margin in percentage points · Q4 guide at its USD 53.3bn midpoint vs. prior consensus · Revenue and margin consensus approximate
C1_COMMENT: The pattern is clear: the top line beat, the margin slipped. Revenue and earnings per share (EPS) both beat consensus by about 3%, and the fourth-quarter guide sits around 6.5% above prior expectations, a 14% sequential step-up. The only miss was gross margin, 0.6 points short at 66.4%, entirely from the 2nm ramp, which should fade as yields improve.
BASE_CASE: We stay positive on TSMC and would add on weakness around the results. We underwrite US dollar revenue growth of 44% in 2026 and an AI business compounding at more than 50% a year; consensus 12-month forward EPS is already up 99% over the past year. The debate has moved from demand to returns: capital spending of USD 60–64bn this year rises sharply in 2027 to 2028, and overseas fabs dilute gross margin by 3–4 points, which analysts expect pricing to cut to about 1 point. Tactically, the American depositary receipt (ADR) sits 13% below its 2 October record. The next test is the fourth-quarter release in mid-January 2027.
UPSIDE: Fourth-quarter gross margin at or above the 67% top of guidance in January; AI accelerator growth confirmed above the mid-to-high 50s% pace; 2nm yields fast enough to lift 2027 capacity beyond the planned doubling; subsidies or customer commitments funding the Dallas complex.
DOWNSIDE: Gross margin below 65%, the bottom of the fourth-quarter guide, and staying there through the 2nm and A14 ramps; capital spending above USD 100bn in 2027 without matching revenue; higher US tariffs on chips; an AI derating that takes the multiple below its 17.0x average.
H_A1: Results: volume beat, 2nm dented the margin
A1_PARAGRAPHS: Third-quarter revenue of USD 46.7bn rose 16.2% quarter on quarter, above guidance, and 41% year on year, about 3% ahead of consensus. High-performance computing (HPC), smartphones and automotive led demand, and the strength was broad rather than a single product cycle. Operating leverage was strong: the operating margin reached 58.7%, ahead of expectations, and EPS of TWD 29.43 beat the TWD 28.67 consensus by 2.7% and rose 69% year on year, in line with net income. This is the third consecutive quarter of beat-and-raise, and it came with an upgrade to the multi-year AI outlook, with agentic AI named as an additional growth engine on top of the cloud AI build-out.

Gross margin was the one soft line. At 66.4% it came in about 0.6 points below elevated expectations of 67% and 1.3 points below the 67.7% of the second quarter, a decline management attributes entirely to the dilution from the 2nm ramp. We read this as a cost of leadership rather than pricing pressure: the dilution was limited for a first-year node, and analysts see it as support for scarcity-driven pricing in 2027. Analyst estimates put 2026 return on equity near 44%, with a net cash balance sheet, so the margin step-down does not constrain the investment plan.
H_A2: Outlook: capacity, not demand, is the limit
A2_PARAGRAPH: The fourth-quarter guide of USD 52.3–54.3bn, with gross margin of 65–67%, implies 44% US dollar revenue growth for 2026. Capital spending stays at USD 60–64bn this year, but 2026 to 2028 spending is guided well above the USD 101bn of the previous three years; analyst estimates range from USD 80–85bn to USD 90bn for 2027 and reach USD 105bn for 2028. Capacity follows: 2nm more than doubles in 2027, Arizona Fab 2 (3nm) starts volume production in the third quarter of 2027, and a Dallas complex could take planned US investment to about USD 530bn. Overseas margin dilution rises from about 2 points in 2026 to 3–4 points in 2027.
H_C2: Valuation: earnings did the work, not the multiple
C2_TITLE: TSM: share price vs. consensus earnings and valuation
C2_SUB: ADR in USD, weekly, April 2005 to 15 October 2026 · Bloomberg 12m-forward consensus EPS in TWD per ADR · 40-week simple moving average · Log scale · Last price is the 15 October (results day) print
C2_COMMENT: Over 12 months the ADR is up 46% to USD 411 while consensus 12-month forward EPS rose 99% to TWD 675 per ADR, so the forward price-to-earnings ratio (P/E) fell from 25.3x to 19.7x. That is 16% above the 17.0x average since 2005, but below the one-year average of 23.3x and the 33.9x peak of February 2021. The price is 13% below its 2 October record and 3% above its 40-week moving average of USD 397. Analysts put the stock at about 16x 2027 earnings; a 10% upgrade at an unchanged price takes the multiple to 17.9x, near its average.
